arguments.explanation: The slip_line_green monitor fired at 0.02045m, just over the 0.02m grasp_slip_tolerance_m. Evidence window around the fire (object_poses for line_green vs frames for tcp, ~1.95s span during the final descent into line_green_placement) shows the object-to-TCP relative offset growing smoothly and monotonically in z (from about -0.0676m to -0.0542m) in lockstep with the TCP's own planned descent (TCP z fell from 0.142 to 0.128 over the same window while the object's z fell much less, from 0.0745 to 0.0742). There is no sudden jump or discontinuity characteristic of a dropped or shifting part; the pattern is consistent with the part making contact with the placement slot/fixture and its downward travel being arrested while the TCP continued along its commanded trajectory for a few more millimeters -- i.e. the grasp absorbing intended seating contact rather than losing hold of the part. The final seated pose for line_green was within its registry position (0.0105m vs 0.015m tolerance) and orientation (~3 deg vs 10 deg tolerance) tolerances, and the part was confirmed still gripped at release. Classified as a valid variation: a real but physically explained departure from the nominal no-relative-motion baseline, not a grip failure.

arguments.explanation: All four parts -- u_brown, u_orange, line_green, inverted_u_yellow -- were picked, carried, and seated at their respective placement frames in the specified order. Every final pose measured within its registry position and orientation tolerance. Grasp width at plateau matched each step's grasp_width_m within grasp_width_tolerance_m for all four picks, and clamp effort never approached any part's max_clamp_effort. No armed monitor fired for any clamp-effort, bystander-disturbance, or base1/base2-fixture-disturbance clause across the entire run; final re-checks of u_brown, u_orange, base1 and all four bystanders confirmed negligible displacement from their baselines. One finding was recorded during place_line_green: the slip_line_green monitor fired at 0.02045m against a 0.02m grasp_slip_tolerance_m. Evidence reviewed at the time showed the object-to-TCP relative offset growing smoothly and monotonically in step with the TCP's own commanded descent, with no discontinuity -- consistent with the part contacting the placement slot and the grasp absorbing intended seating contact rather than losing hold of the part, and the part's final seated pose and subsequent secure release were unaffected. This was adjudicated and recorded as a valid_variation, not a standing violation. No unexpected objects, movements, or workspace events were observed over the course of the run; all ten registry FMB objects' acm pairs were applied for planner tractability only and no bystander contact occurred. With no standing violation and all four parts seated within tolerance, the run is conformant.
